lead_headline: AI SDK races a May 26 deadline while Claude Code accumulates a day's worth of bug reports
lead_body: Thirty commits landed in AI SDK today, anchoring on a patch for Google's Interactions API before its upstream breaking change hits on May 26. Claude Code shipped v2.1.143 quietly but opened six bug reports by day's end, including a 429-into-400 retry spiral that leaves sessions unrecoverable and a Task tool gap that collapses multi-agent orchestration to single-agent execution. Metaflow drew a security disclosure — four findings, one an RCE claim — low in volume, not in consequence.
lead_article:
The busiest signal today belongs to AI SDK, which pushed thirty commits against a hard deadline: Google's Interactions API is breaking upstream on May 26, and the patch landed at 21:41 to absorb that change before it lands. Alongside it, native structured output was quietly disabled for claude-opus-4-7 on Amazon Bedrock — apparently it misbehaves there — and OpenAI gained an opt-in passthrough for unsupported file media types, a small but meaningful escape hatch for edge-case media handling. GitHub Actions pins moved to commit SHAs across the board, a supply-chain hygiene sweep that deserves a nod even if it reads like plumbing. Workflow SDK had a focused day of its own: the VQS handler retry landed at 20:17, and three CI files migrated to gh-sts for scoped token minting, trimming the default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions down to what's actually needed.

Claude Code cut a quiet v2.1.143 but is accumulating bug reports at a pace worth watching — six opened today alone, touching session auto-archiving, a 429-into-400 retry spiral that leaves sessions unrecoverable, background agents stuck in working state, and the Task tool being unavailable inside sub-agents, which effectively collapses multi-role orchestrators to single-agent execution. Astro had eighteen commits across CI repair work, a deprecation removal for astro:transitions internals, and a late PR to fix syntax highlighting after CSS @property rules. Metaflow drew a security disclosure — four findings including an RCE claim — which is the quietest item in volume but not in consequence.
